walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Presentation & Interpretation — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Presentation & Interpretation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Presentation & Interpretation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which average is most affected by extreme outliers?
options: mean
median
mode
range

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of any pentagon?
options: It means the vectors are parallel.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
540 degrees — use (n - 2) x 180 with n = 5.
360 degrees, because all polygons' angles sum to one full turn.

mcqs.q: If the dot product of two non-zero vectors is zero, what does that mean?
options: It means the vectors are parallel.
The vectors are perpendicular to each other.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
It means at least one of the vectors is the zero vector.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of (3x + 1)^2 with respect to x?
options: The derivative is 2(3x + 1) — applying the power rule without the chain rule.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
6(3x + 1) — by the chain rule, multiplying by the derivative of the inside (3).
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Outliers”?
options: Show min, Q₁, median, Q₃, max. Visualise spread, skew, outliers. Useful for comparing distributions.
Values far from the rest. Common rule: outside Q₁ − 1.5·IQR or Q₃ + 1.5·IQR. May skew mean.
Running total. Plotting against upper class boundary gives an S-curve, used to estimate medians and quartiles.
Mean = sum/n. Median = middle value of ordered data. Mode = most frequent value. Different averages, different uses.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cumulative frequency”?
options: Values far from the rest. Common rule: outside Q₁ − 1.5·IQR or Q₃ + 1.5·IQR. May skew mean.
Running total. Plotting against upper class boundary gives an S-curve, used to estimate medians and quartiles.
Mean = sum/n. Median = middle value of ordered data. Mode = most frequent value. Different averages, different uses.
Range = max − min. IQR = Q₃ − Q₁ (middle 50% spread). Standard deviation σ = √(variance), more sensitive measure.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Range, IQR, SD”?
options: Values far from the rest. Common rule: outside Q₁ − 1.5·IQR or Q₃ + 1.5·IQR. May skew mean.

Show min, Q₁, median, Q₃, max. Visualise spread, skew, outliers. Useful for comparing distributions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sampling”?
options: Range = max − min. IQR = Q₃ − Q₁ (middle 50% spread). Standard deviation σ = √(variance), more sensitive measure.
Random, stratified, systematic, opportunity, quota. Aim: representative of population without bias.
Mean = sum/n. Median = middle value of ordered data. Mode = most frequent value. Different averages, different uses.
Running total. Plotting against upper class boundary gives an S-curve, used to estimate medians and quartiles.

sequence.def: Collect raw data from a population sample — the first step.
Summarise the centre of the data with averages.
Measure how spread out the data is.
Flag extreme values using the spread measures.
Running totals up each class — used to read quartiles.
Drawn from quartiles to display spread visually — final summary.
